newsitem.title: LEBANON: SOLIDERE shares rise in Beirut. [CORRECTED 10:45 GMT]
newsitem.headline: SOLIDERE shares rise in Beirut. [CORRECTED 10:45 GMT]

text.p: SOLIDERE shares rose on Wednesday on the Beirut Secondary Market (BSM) for the sixth day running due to expectations that the company plans to launch a $150 million GDR issue, dealers said.
A shares rose to $115 from Tuesday's $114.625 on the privately-operated BSM and B shares rose to $117.125 (Corrects from $118) from $116.375.

Dealers say momentum is building up on the Beirut equities market because of expectations that SOLIDERE will launch a $150 million Global Depositary Receipts issue in mid-October, giving non-Arab investors access to the market for the first time.
SOLIDERE declined to comment on the report which followed rumours on the Beirut market.
Turnover on the BSM, which trades only SOLIDERE shares, fell to 15,246 from Tuesday's 20,036 shares and value was $1,767,433 from $2,296,841.
On the Beirut Stock Exchange (BSE), Ciments Libanais held steady at $1.375 on sale of 1,500 shares.
There was no trade in any of the other listed companies: Ciments Blancs, Eternit, and Uniceramic.
The LISPI index rose 0.41 percent to 85.59 and the BLOM index rose 0.38 percent to 997.51. They cover both markets.
